scheme_name: National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture - Reinforced Area Development
description:
The National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture is a significant initiative launched by the Government of India in 2010 under the National Action Plan on Climate Change.

This mission aims to promote sustainable agricultural practices that enhance productivity while ensuring environmental sustainability.

The Reinforced Area Development component of this mission focuses on improving agricultural productivity in rainfed areas.

The primary objective of this initiative is to increase the productivity of crops in these vulnerable regions by 20 to 25 percent over a period of five years.

This target is to be achieved through the adoption of climate-resilient agricultural practices and technologies.

The mission emphasizes the importance of soil health management and integrated nutrient management.

It also aims to promote efficient water management practices to ensure optimal use of available water resources.

The initiative seeks to enhance the income of farmers by promoting sustainable farming practices that reduce dependency on chemical fertilizers and pesticides.

The mission is designed to benefit approximately 5 crore farmers across the country.

It aims to cover around 10 million hectares of rainfed agricultural land.

The financial allocation for the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture in the 2021-2022 budget was approximately INR 1,000 crore.

The scheme provides various benefits to farmers including financial assistance for the adoption of sustainable agricultural practices.

Farmers can receive up to INR 20,000 per hectare for implementing soil health management practices.

Additionally, they can receive financial support for the establishment of rainwater harvesting structures.

The mission also promotes the use of organic fertilizers and bio-pesticides.

Farmers are encouraged to participate in training programs that focus on sustainable agricultural practices.

The eligibility criteria for farmers to benefit from this scheme include being a resident of India and actively engaged in agricultural activities.

Farmers must also demonstrate a commitment to adopting sustainable practices.

There are no specific age limits for eligibility under this scheme.

However, farmers must have a valid landholding to qualify for financial assistance.

The application process for the Reinforced Area Development component involves several steps.

Farmers must first register with the local agricultural department.

They need to submit an application form along with necessary documents such as proof of land ownership and identity proof.

The required documents typically include an Aadhaar card and land revenue records.

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by the local agricultural officer.

Farmers may be required to attend a training session before receiving financial assistance.

The disbursement of funds is typically made directly to the bank account of the farmer.

The timeline for the application process can vary but generally takes about 30 to 45 days from submission to fund disbursement.

The mission is implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare.

The National Rainfed Area Authority is also involved in the implementation of this mission.

Farmers can contact the local agricultural department for more information about the scheme.

The contact details of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare can be found on their official website.

The mission has seen various success stories across different states in India.

For example, in Madhya Pradesh, farmers have reported increased yields of up to 30 percent after adopting practices promoted under this mission.

In Rajasthan, the establishment of rainwater harvesting structures has significantly improved water availability for agriculture.

The mission also emphasizes the importance of crop diversification.

Farmers are encouraged to cultivate a variety of crops to reduce risks associated with climate change.

The initiative promotes the use of drought-resistant crop varieties.

It provides training on integrated pest management techniques.

The mission also supports the establishment of farmer producer organizations.

These organizations help farmers in marketing their produce and accessing better prices.

The mission aims to create awareness about sustainable agricultural practices among farmers.

It also seeks to enhance the capacity of agricultural extension services.

The mission is aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals set by the United Nations.

It aims to promote food security and sustainable agriculture.

The mission also focuses on improving the livelihoods of small and marginal farmers.

The government has set a target to increase the area under sustainable agricultural practices to 20 million hectares by 2025.

The mission encourages the use of technology in agriculture.

Farmers are provided with access to information on weather forecasts and market prices.

The mission also promotes the use of mobile applications for better farm management.

The government conducts regular assessments to monitor the progress of the mission.

The National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture is part of a larger strategy to combat climate change.

It aims to ensure that agriculture remains resilient in the face of changing climatic conditions.

The mission also addresses issues related to soil degradation and water scarcity.

It promotes practices that enhance soil fertility and water conservation.

The mission has received positive feedback from various stakeholders in the agricultural sector.

Farmers have reported improved resilience to climate-related shocks after adopting sustainable practices.

The mission is expected to play a crucial role in achieving the goal of doubling farmers' income by 2022.

The government continues to seek innovative solutions to enhance the effectiveness of this mission.

The National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture represents a comprehensive approach to transforming Indian agriculture.

It aims to create a sustainable and resilient agricultural sector that can withstand the challenges posed by climate change.

The mission is a testament to the government's commitment to promoting sustainable development in agriculture.
